itens.t: SpaceX Catches Starship Upper Stage for First Time Ever in Historic Milestone
itens.r: SpaceX successfully captured the upper stage of its massive Starship megarocket using launchpad mechanical arms for the first time ever. The landmark achievement occurred at the conclusion of an ambitious 22-hour orbital test flight launched from Starbase in Texas. Company officials highlighted that the successful midair catch demonstrates full reusability for the upper stage. This technological leap is considered crucial for enabling rapid, low-cost space recycling and future deep-space missions.
itens.d:
SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today at Starbase in South Texas. The milestone occurred during Starship's 15th test flight, roughly 22.5 hours after liftoff.

While the Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown due to a low-fuel alarm, the Ship successfully executed its descent. Employees watched as Ship 42 was snatched out of the air by the launch tower's mechanical arms, marking a historic achievement for full rocket reuse.
itens.e:
SpaceX achieved a historic milestone today at Starbase in South Texas by successfully catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time during its 15th test flight. Although the Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown due to a low-fuel alarm roughly 22.5 hours after liftoff, employees watched as Ship 42 was snatched out of the air by the launch tower's mechanical arms.

This success represents a major step forward for full rocket reuse, directly impacting the aerospace industry and future launch economics. This suggests that mechanical retrieval systems are becoming increasingly viable for large-scale aerospace operations, moving the industry closer to rapid turnaround capabilities.

One risk is that unexpected anomalies, such as the low-fuel alarm that forced the booster's water landing, could still impede testing schedules. Observers should watch how SpaceX addresses these booster diversion issues in subsequent test flights to gauge the true reliability of the system.

itens.t: Kim Jong Un's Top Aide Visits Russia Ahead of High-Stakes Summit

The high-level diplomatic visit comes just days before a historic three-way summit involving the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia. Jo Yong-won, a secretary of the ruling Workers' Party, led a party and government delegation to Moscow at the invitation of Dmitry Medvedev. The visit has raised concerns in Seoul that Pyongyang might seek recognition of its nuclear status while South Korea is sidelined.
itens.e:
Jo Yong-won, the closest aide to North Korean leader Kim Jong-un and a secretary of the ruling Workers' Party, arrived in Russia on Saturday leading a party and government delegation. This visit occurred at the invitation of Dmitry Medvedev ahead of a historic three-way summit involving the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia.

The diplomatic maneuvering has raised serious concerns in Seoul that Pyongyang might seek recognition of its nuclear status while South Korea is left on the sidelines. This suggests that regional power dynamics are shifting, potentially altering the diplomatic leverage of nations traditionally involved in Korean Peninsula security discussions.

One risk is that sidelined nations may face new strategic realities following the high-stakes summit. Observers must watch whether Pyongyang successfully leverages the meetings to secure international acknowledgment of its nuclear ambitions while excluding Seoul.

itens.r: South Korean League of Legends powerhouse Gen.G fell to China's Bilibili Gaming in the 2026 World Championship final. The defeat snaps South Korea's four-year reign as world champions in the esports discipline.
itens.d:
South Korean powerhouse Gen.G fell to China's Bilibili Gaming 1-3 in the 2026 League of Legends World Championship final at New York's Barclays Center. After winning the opening game, the Korean squad lost three consecutive matches.

The defeat snapped Korea's four-year streak as world champions, returning the title to China for the first time in five years. The loss also denied Gen.G its first world championship in nine years.
itens.e:
South Korean powerhouse Gen.G fell to China's Bilibili Gaming with a score of 1-3 in the 2026 League of Legends World Championship final at New York's Barclays Center. After taking the opening game, the Korean squad lost three consecutive matches, snapping Korea's four-year streak as world champions and denying Gen.G its first world title in nine years.

This defeat returns the championship title to China for the first time in five years, significantly impacting the competitive landscape of professional esports. This suggests that the balance of power in international League of Legends is shifting away from South Korean dominance toward Chinese organizations.

One risk for the defeated region is a loss of competitive prestige in the global esports ecosystem. Observers should watch how Korean teams restructure their training and strategies ahead of future international competitions to counter the rising dominance of Chinese squads.

Han answered 159 of 160 questions correctly in the first-stage exam in April and later scored 663 out of 800 in the written second stage. Experts had previously argued that his near-perfect first test score was close to impossible.

itens.t: Stargazers Prepare for Spectacular Close Planetary Approach of Mars and Jupiter
itens.r: Stargazers worldwide are gearing up to observe a rare celestial conjunction where Mars and Jupiter will appear exceptionally close together in the night sky.
itens.d:
Stargazers are preparing for a close planetary approach of Mars and Jupiter in the constellation Leo on the night of November 15-16. The two planets will appear just over 1 degree apart as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight in the U.S., with the star Regulus glowing below.

This celestial event, known as an appulse, occurs every 2 to 2.5 years when Mars catches up to Jupiter in its distant orbit. Through a telescope, observers can view Jupiter's distinct cloud bands and the full disks of both superior planets.

itens.t: VIDEO: Live Footage and Reaction of the First-Ever Orbital Starship Catch
itens.r: Exciting video documentation capturing the historic moment SpaceX successfully caught its towering Starship upper stage with mechanical launchpad arms.
itens.d:

itens.t: Warming Ocean Waters Cause 99% Collapse in Ulleung Island Squid Catch
itens.r: Rising sea temperatures driven by climate change have decimated the squid population around South Korea's Ulleung Island over the past 25 years.
itens.d:
The squid catch around Ulleung Island has collapsed by 99 percent due to rising sea temperatures linked to climate change. Local records show catches dropped from 11,315 tons in 2000 down to just 141 tons in 2025, with only 54 tons caught through September of this year.

Squid has long been the signature seafood and economic mainstay of the island. According to the National Institute of Fisheries Science, warming waters in the East Sea have pushed the squid population further north toward Russia.

itens.t: NASA Celebrates Anniversary of Historic Apollo 12 Pinpoint Lunar Landing
itens.r: Space historians are reflecting on the legacy of NASA's Apollo 12 mission, which successfully achieved a precision lunar landing in November 1969.
itens.d:
NASA is celebrating the anniversary of the Apollo 12 mission, which launched to the moon on November 14, 1969. Commander Pete Conrad and lunar module pilot Alan Bean achieved a precise landing in the Ocean of Storms near the robotic lander Surveyor 3.

The mission allowed astronauts to examine Surveyor 3 and collect 75 pounds of moon rocks, mostly basalts indicating the site is over 3 billion years old. Apollo 12 proved the success of Apollo 11 was not an isolated event and enabled targeted geological exploration.
